extracted.subtask_description: Practical public-relations guidance and checklists for founders pre-Series A on when to do PR, how to craft stories and press releases, pitching reporters, distribution tactics, and basic crisis response.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR objectives / Why PR now
rubrics_metrics.description: Builds inbound pipeline (talent, customers, investors); creates social proof for cold outreach; differentiates in a crowded market; long-term reputation asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PR to drive inbound interest across hires/customers/investors, to add credibility when reaching out cold, and to create sustainable differentiation and reputation value over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: When PR doesn't help
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where PR is not appropriate: pre-product; pre-product-market-fit (pre-PMF); during stealth periods; when competing on price (not differentiation); when the team can't sustain media obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid major PR pushes if you lack a product or PMF, are intentionally in stealth, are competing only on price (no newsworthy differentiation), or if your team cannot respond to media requests and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder's PR toolkit — email outreach template
rubrics_metrics.description: Have an email outreach template ready as part of your toolkit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use templates as a starting point but personalize heavily per reporter (see pitching rules). Templates should be concise and support personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder's PR toolkit — press release template (use sparingly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a press release template, but use it sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases are one tool among many; reserve releases for genuine newsworthy events and rely primarily on targeted outreach for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder's PR toolkit — HARO / Connectively for source-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Use HARO and Connectively to build relationships as a source for journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor relevant HARO queries and proactively offer subject-matter expertise to reporters to become a relied-upon source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder's PR toolkit — Muck Rack for journalist research
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Muck Rack to research and identify relevant journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use journalist research tools to build an informed, relevant reporter list and understand beats and recent coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder's PR toolkit — LinkedIn for direct outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Use LinkedIn as a channel for direct outreach to journalists and amplifying news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement email outreach with LinkedIn engagement where appropriate; use for follow-ups and amplification of earned coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story development — core elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Key story elements to develop: What's the founding story? What problem are you solving? What's the surprising insight you have? What's the data you uniquely possess? What's the human angle?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame press narratives around these five elements; combine an emotional human angle with unique data or insights to increase newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching reporters — size of reporter list
rubrics_metrics.description: Build list of 20 relevant reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a targeted short list (around 20) of reporters most likely to care about your story rather than mass-blasting dozens; quality over quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching reporters — reporter familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Read 5+ articles per reporter before pitching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand a reporter's beat and recent work by reading multiple articles so your pitch is genuinely tailored and shows awareness of their coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching reporters — personalize first email
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalize the first email to each reporter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the opening reference specific to the reporter's prior coverage or interests; avoid generic outreach that shows no knowledge of their beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching reporters — subject line guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line: news + entity in 8 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep subject lines tight and news-focused; include the key news hook and the entity (company) within about eight words to convey relevance quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching reporters — email length guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Body: 100-200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the pitch concise (100–200 words), front-load the news, and make it scannable so reporters can grasp the story fast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching reporters — single clear ask
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a single clear ask in your pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the reporter exactly what you want (e.g., an interview, background, embargoed comment) to remove ambiguity and make it easy to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching reporters — provide phone number
rubrics_metrics.description: Phone number provided in the pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include a direct phone number to enable quick follow-up and to signal availability and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release anatomy — headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline: news first, brand second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write headlines that lead with the news hook; brand mentions should be secondary to maximize journalist and reader interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release anatomy — lede
rubrics_metrics.description: Lede: 5 W's in 50 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with who, what, when, where, why (and how if relevant) within about 50 words to make the news obvious immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release anatomy — body structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Body: 3–4 paragraphs in an inverted pyramid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present most important information first, then supporting details; keep releases short and structured for quick scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release anatomy — quote length & source
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote: 25–35 words from founder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a concise 25–35 word quote, ideally from the founder, that adds color or perspective without repeating factual details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release anatomy — boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate: 50 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a brief 50-word company boilerplate giving context about the business, mission, and quick facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release anatomy — contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact: founder direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List a founder (or direct company spokesperson) as the contact to signal accessibility and seriousness; include direct phone/email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release anatomy — end marker
rubrics_metrics.description: "###" end marker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminate the release with the conventional '###' marker so journalists recognize the end of the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution tactics — direct outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct outreach for actual coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize targeted, personalized outreach to reporters for earned coverage rather than relying solely on wires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution tactics — wire for SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Use wire distribution for SEO purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider press wires primarily to boost discoverability and SEO; wires are less effective for generating direct earned coverage than reporter outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution tactics — LinkedIn for amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use LinkedIn for amplification of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share and promote coverage and announcements on LinkedIn to reach professional networks and amplify earned media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution tactics — newsletter inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue newsletter inclusion as an amplification channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target relevant industry newsletters to reach niche, engaged audiences who may not see mainstream coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution tactics — podcast appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Use podcast appearances to tell the story and reach new audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue podcast interviews to provide depth, humanize the founder, and reach engaged listeners; prepare storylines and soundbites accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis response checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis basics: acknowledge within 2 hours; state specific facts; name accountability; outline concrete actions; establish update cadence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapidly acknowledge incidents, communicate verified facts, assign and name who is accountable, state concrete remedial actions, and promise regular updates on a clear cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — founder is spokesperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder is spokesperson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer founders as the public face for early-stage PR to provide authenticity and direct access for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — story types match stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Story types match stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose story angles appropriate to company stage (e.g., product milestones for early-stage, growth metrics for later-stage) to increase relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — personalized pitching
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized pitching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure outreach quality by the degree of personalization and reporter fit rather than volume of outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — multimedia ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have images, video, and other multimedia assets prepared to support coverage and make it easier for reporters to use your story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — press release as one tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release as one tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat press releases as one part of a broader PR strategy—use them judiciously alongside targeted outreach and amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — crisis protocol established
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis protocol established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a documented crisis protocol exists (acknowledgement timelines, spokespeople, messaging workflow, and update cadence) before issues arise.
